title: StubHub International tells customers contact data may have been exposed
summary: StubHub International, run by Ticketbis S.L., emailed customers after detecting unauthorised access to certain systems between late October and early November. Names, email addresses, phone numbers and country settings may have been exposed. The company says it found no evidence of access to passwords, banking or card details. The number of customers affected has not been given.
plain: A ticket resale site warned customers that their names, emails and phone numbers may have leaked. It says no payment details were taken.
exec: Exposed contact details enable convincing phishing against ticket buyers.
action: Customers: treat unexpected messages claiming to be StubHub with suspicion and do not click links.
date_note: Date is the publication date of The Register's report; HQ country inferred from the Ticketbis S.L. company form, not stated by sources.

validation.note: The Register read; LavX News repeats it. Company notification emails seen by The Register.

review.note: Compared data types, late Oct-early Nov window, no password/payment evidence, no count, Ticketbis S.L. against The Register; LavX is a rewrite so single_source is right; Spain pin inference disclosed in date_note
